name: Arks of Omen Grand Tournament
source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k9ed/the-rules/arks-of-omen-grand-tournament/ (Arks of Omen: Grand Tournament Games, steps 1-16; Secondary Objectives), retrieved 2026-10-22

setupSteps.name: 1. Select battle size
setupSteps.text: Pick Incursion (1,000 points, up to 2 hours) or Strike Force (2,000 points, up to 3 hours).

setupSteps.name: 2. Muster armies
setupSteps.text: Each player builds a Battle-forged army with exactly one Arks of Omen Detachment, plus at most one Allied Detachment that the Battle Brothers rules allow. Each player starts with 6 CP, which can buy Requisition Stratagems such as Warlord Trait and Relic. Each datasheet can appear at most 2 times in Incursion and 3 times in Strike Force, except Troops, Dedicated Transports and units added during the battle. Swap army rosters with your opponent.

setupSteps.name: 3. Determine mission
setupSteps.text: Agree on a mission for your battle size, or roll a D33: roll two D3s, the first is the tens and the second the units.

setupSteps.name: 4. Read mission briefing
setupSteps.text: Read the mission rules and the primary objective together.

setupSteps.name: 5. Place objective markers
setupSteps.text: Set up the objective markers where the deployment map shows.

setupSteps.name: 6. Create the battlefield
setupSteps.text: Set up terrain on a battlefield of at least 44" x 30" for Incursion or 44" x 60" for Strike Force. Terrain can't be set up on top of objective markers.

setupSteps.name: 7. Determine Attacker and Defender
setupSteps.text: Roll off. The winner decides who is the Attacker and who is the Defender.

setupSteps.name: 8. Choose deployment zone
setupSteps.text: The Defender picks a deployment zone. The Attacker takes the other one.

setupSteps.name: 9. Select secondary objectives
setupSteps.text: Each player secretly writes down 3 secondary objectives, then both reveal them. If you don't pick your own, you use Assassination, Grind Them Down and Behind Enemy Lines. You can't take more than one from the same category, and you can't use secondary objectives from a Codex or Codex supplement.

setupSteps.name: 10. Declare reserves and transports
setupSteps.text: Each player secretly notes which units start in Strategic Reserves (this costs no CP in these missions; Fortifications can't go there), which start somewhere other than the battlefield, and which start embarked in which TRANSPORT. Each Dedicated Transport must start with at least one model embarked, or it can't be set up and counts as destroyed in the first battle round. Then both players reveal their notes. No more than half your units can be Strategic Reserve or Reinforcement units, and together they must be worth less than half your army's points. These units can't arrive in the first battle round, and any that haven't arrived by the end of the third battle round count as destroyed, along with anything embarked in them.

setupSteps.name: 11. Deploy armies
setupSteps.text: Take turns setting up one unit at a time, starting with the Defender. Set up your Fortifications before anything else. Models must be wholly within your deployment zone. A model too big to fit must touch your battlefield edge, and its unit can't move, shoot, charge, manifest powers or do actions in the first battle round.

setupSteps.name: 12. Determine first turn
setupSteps.text: Roll off. The winner takes the first turn.

setupSteps.name: 13. Resolve pre-battle abilities
setupSteps.text: Take turns resolving pre-battle abilities and Stratagems used before the battle, starting with the player who takes the first turn.

setupSteps.name: 14. Begin the battle
setupSteps.text: Play battle rounds until the battle ends.

setupSteps.name: 15. Ending the battle
setupSteps.text: The battle ends after 5 battle rounds. If a player has no models left at the start of their turn, the other player can keep playing their turns until the end.

setupSteps.name: 16. Determine victor
setupSteps.text: The player with the most VP wins; equal VP is a draw. You can score at most 45 VP from the primary objective and 15 VP from each secondary objective, plus 10 VP if your whole army is painted to a Battle Ready standard. If one player concedes, their opponent wins.

setupSteps.name: 1. Select battle size
setupSteps.text: Pick Combat Patrol (500 points, up to 1 hour) or Onslaught (3,000 points, up to 4 hours).

setupSteps.name: 2. Muster armies
setupSteps.text: Each player builds a Battle-forged army. You start with 3 CP in Combat Patrol or 18 CP in Onslaught, and Detachments spend some of it. No Understrength units. In Combat Patrol your only Detachment is one Patrol Detachment (Imperial Knights and Chaos Knights use one Super-heavy Detachment instead). Each datasheet can appear at most 3 times, except Troops, Dedicated Transports and units that cost Reinforcement points. Use any Stratagems that upgrade units now, then swap army rosters with your opponent.

setupSteps.name: 3. Determine mission
setupSteps.text: Agree on a mission for your battle size, or roll a D6 on its mission table.

setupSteps.name: 4. Read mission briefing
setupSteps.text: Read the primary objectives, any mission rules and any mission secondary objective together.

setupSteps.name: 5. Place objective markers
setupSteps.text: Set up the objective markers where the deployment map shows.

setupSteps.name: 6. Create the battlefield
setupSteps.text: Set up terrain on a battlefield of at least 44" x 30" for Combat Patrol or 44" x 90" for Onslaught. Terrain can't be set up on top of objective markers.

setupSteps.name: 7. Select secondary objectives
setupSteps.text: Each player secretly writes down 3 secondary objectives, then both reveal them. You can't take more than one from the same category. The mission may offer its own secondary objective as one of your three.

setupSteps.name: 8. Determine Attacker and Defender
setupSteps.text: Roll off. The winner decides who is the Attacker and who is the Defender.

setupSteps.name: 9. Choose deployment zone
setupSteps.text: The Defender picks a deployment zone. The Attacker takes the other one.

setupSteps.name: 10. Declare reserves and transports
setupSteps.text: Each player secretly notes which units start in Strategic Reserves, which start somewhere other than the battlefield, and which start embarked in which TRANSPORT. Then both players reveal their notes. No more than half your units can be Strategic Reserve or Reinforcement units, and together they must be worth less than half your army's points. These units can't arrive in the first battle round, and any that haven't arrived by the end of the third battle round count as destroyed, along with anything embarked in them.

setupSteps.name: 11. Deploy armies
setupSteps.text: Take turns setting up one unit at a time, starting with the Defender. Models must be wholly within your deployment zone. A model too big to fit must touch your battlefield edge, and its unit can't move, shoot, charge, manifest powers or do actions in the first battle round.

setupSteps.name: 12. Determine first turn
setupSteps.text: Roll off. The winner chooses whether to take the first or the second turn.

setupSteps.name: 13. Resolve pre-battle abilities
setupSteps.text: Take turns resolving pre-battle abilities and Stratagems used before the battle, starting with the player who takes the first turn.

setupSteps.name: 14. Begin the battle
setupSteps.text: Play battle rounds until the battle ends.

setupSteps.name: 15. Ending the battle
setupSteps.text: The battle ends after 5 battle rounds. If a player has no models left at the start of their turn, the other player can keep playing their turns until the end.

setupSteps.name: 16. Determine victor
setupSteps.text: The player with the most VP wins; equal VP is a draw. You can score at most 45 VP from primary objectives and 15 VP from each secondary objective, plus 10 VP if your whole army is painted to a Battle Ready standard. A player who concedes scores 0 VP and their opponent wins.
